paras.t: Quod in præsentis capituli exordio ad litteram dictum est de Synagoga, spiritualiter de Christi Ecclesia et qualibet anima christiana accipi potest. Itaque Dominus ait: Zelatus sum Sion, id est Ecclesiam, seu animam christifidelem, zelo magno. Ipsa enim est sponsa Christi, qui ex amore suo ad eam factus est homo pro ea, et proprio ipsam sanguine liberavit: ad quam ait in Canticis, Vulnerasti cor meum, soror mea, sponsa. Propter quod ad Ephesios dicit Apostolus: Christus dilexit Ecclesiam, et tradidit semetipsum pro ea, ut illam sanctificaret. Sed et ipsemet Christus in Joanne protestatur: Sicut dilexit me Pater, et ego dilexi vos. Et indignatione magna zelatus sum eam, quoniam quo eam plus diligo, eo peccata illius amplius odio, et statim castigationem adhibeo: juxta illud Apocalypsis, Ego quos amo, arguo et castigo.
paras.en: What was said literally at the opening of the present chapter about the Synagogue can be taken spiritually of the Church of Christ and of every Christian soul. Thus the Lord says: [[8:2|I have been jealous for Sion|Zelatus sum Sion]], that is, for the Church, or for the soul faithful to Christ, [[8:2|with a great jealousy|zelo magno]]. For she is the spouse of Christ, who out of his love for her was made man for her sake, and set her free with his own blood; to whom he says in the Canticles: [[Cant 4:9|Thou hast wounded my heart, my sister, my spouse|Vulnerasti cor meum, soror mea, sponsa]]. On which account the Apostle says to the Ephesians: [[Eph 5:25|Christ also loved the church and delivered himself up for it|Christus dilexit Ecclesiam, et tradidit semetipsum pro ea]], [[Eph 5:26|That he might sanctify it|ut illam sanctificaret]]. And Christ himself also declares in John: [[John 15:9|As the Father hath loved me, I also have loved you|Sicut dilexit me Pater, et ego dilexi vos]]. [[8:2|and with a great indignation have I been jealous for her|Et indignatione magna zelatus sum eam]], because the more I love her, the more I hate her sins, and at once I apply chastisement: according to that word of the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 3:19|Such as I love, I rebuke and chastise|Ego quos amo, arguo et castigo]].

paras.t: Hæc dicit Dominus: Reversus sum ad Sion, quoniam pœnitentem clementer recipio, gratiamque refundo. Imo nondum pœnitentem Christus frequenter piissime prævenit, ad bona instigat, ad gratiam aptat, spiritualiter visitat, et operi manuum suarum in vitiorum cœno jacenti, adjutricem porrigit manum, de lacu miseriæ et de luto fæcis ipsam educens. Et habitabo in medio Jerusalem, id est in pectore animæ seu Ecclesiæ, divinæ pacis visioni fideliter inhiantis. Ideo orat Apostolus: Det vobis secundum divitias gloriæ suæ, virtutem corroborari in interiori homine per Spiritum Sanctum, habitare Christum per fidem in cordibus vestris. Et vocabitur Jerusalem, id est Ecclesia, civitas veritatis, videlicet Christi, qui ait: Ego sum via, veritas, et vita. De qua fertur in Psalmo: Gloriosa dicta sunt de te, civitas Dei. In Ecclesia nempe est unio civium: quibus scribit Apostolus, Jam non estis hospites et advenæ, sed estis cives Sanctorum et domestici Dei. Anima quoque justi, civitas Christi censetur: quia in ea est cogitationum et affectionum, tanquam civium, sub rationis imperio ordinata consensio; et mons sanctificatus, propter contemplationis sublimitatem, vitæ eminentiam, gratiæ apicem. De quibus civitate ac monte ad Hebræos legitur: Accessistis ad montem Sion, et civitatem Dei viventis, Jerusalem cœlestem.
paras.en: [[8:3|Thus saith the Lord|Hæc dicit Dominus]]: [[8:3|I am returned to Sion|Reversus sum ad Sion]], because I mercifully receive the penitent, and pour grace back into him. Nay more, Christ often most lovingly goes before the soul not yet penitent, urges it to good, fits it for grace, visits it spiritually, and to the work of his hands lying in the mire of vices he reaches out a helping hand[[Job 14:15||]], leading it out [[Ps 39:3|of the pit of misery and the mire of dregs|de lacu miseriæ et de luto fæcis]]. [[8:3|and I will dwell in the midst of Jerusalem|Et habitabo in medio Jerusalem]], that is, in the breast of the soul or of the Church, faithfully longing for the vision of divine peace [Jerusalem being interpreted *vision of peace*]. Therefore the Apostle prays: [[Eph 3:16|That he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory, to be strengthened by his Spirit with might unto the inward man|Det vobis secundum divitias gloriæ suæ, virtutem corroborari in interiori homine per Spiritum Sanctum]], [[Eph 3:17|That Christ may dwell by faith in your hearts|habitare Christum per fidem in cordibus vestris]]. [[8:3|and Jerusalem shall be called|Et vocabitur Jerusalem]], that is, the Church, [[8:3|The city of truth|civitas veritatis]], namely of Christ, who says: [[John 14:6|I am the way, and the truth, and the life|Ego sum via, veritas, et vita]]. Of which it is said in the Psalm: [[Ps 86:3|Glorious things are said of thee, O city of God|Gloriosa dicta sunt de te, civitas Dei]]. For in the Church there is the union of citizens, to whom the Apostle writes: [[Eph 2:19|you are no more strangers and foreigners: but you are fellow citizens with the saints and the domestics of God|Jam non estis hospites et advenæ, sed estis cives Sanctorum et domestici Dei]]. The soul of the just man, too, is reckoned a city of Christ, because in it there is an ordered agreement of thoughts and affections, as of citizens, under the rule of reason; and [[8:3|The sanctified mountain|mons sanctificatus]], because of the sublimity of its contemplation, the eminence of its life, the summit of its grace. Of which city and mountain we read in the Epistle to the Hebrews: [[Heb 12:22|you are come to mount Sion and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem|Accessistis ad montem Sion, et civitatem Dei viventis, Jerusalem cœlestem]].

paras.t: Hæc dicit Dominus: Adhuc habitabunt senes et anus, id est in virtutum perfectione maturi, animo graves, in virtutibus exercitati: quibus lacte opus non est, sed solidum queunt capere cibum; qui tentationibus probati sunt atque experti. Unde in Sapientiæ libro habetur: Senectus venerabilis est, non diuturna, neque annorum numero computata; cani autem sunt sensus hominis, et ætas senectutis, vita immaculata. Verum, ut Isaias asserit: Puer centum annorum morietur. De hujuscemodi senibus scriptum est in Ecclesiastico: Non te prætereat narratio seniorum. Hi moriuntur in senectute bona, senes et pleni dierum. Anus quoque sunt simili modo accipiendæ: quæ et aliorum matres digne possunt vocari. De qualibus dicit Apostolus: Viduas honora, quæ vere viduæ sunt. Hi itaque habitabunt, id est, stabiliter vivent ac permanebunt, in plateis Jerusalem, in divinis præceptis atque consiliis, in virtutibus cunctis, præsertim in caritate Dei ac proximi. Per has plateas ad æternam illam supercœlestem Jerusalem itur et pervenitur. Unde et scriptum est in Psalmo: Statuisti in loco spatioso pedes meos; et, Latum mandatum tuum nimis. Sponsa quoque in Canticis per vicos et plateas quærit quem diligit. Nec obstat, quod arcta est via quæ ducit ad vitam: arcta est equidem, quia difficulter in ea persistitur; et lata, quia ut regia via omnes capere potest, et per caritatem ad universos, etiam ad adversarios, se extendit.
paras.en: [[8:4|Thus saith the Lord|Hæc dicit Dominus]]: [[8:4|There shall yet old men and old women dwell|Adhuc habitabunt senes et anus]], that is, those ripe in the perfection of the virtues, grave of mind, practised in the virtues: who have no need of milk, but can take solid food[[Heb 5:12||]]; who have been proved and tried by temptations. Hence it is said in the book of Wisdom: [[Wis 4:8|venerable old age is not that of long time, nor counted by the number of years: but the understanding of a man is grey hairs|Senectus venerabilis est, non diuturna, neque annorum numero computata; cani autem sunt sensus hominis]], [[Wis 4:9|And a spotless life is old age|et ætas senectutis, vita immaculata]]. Indeed, as Isaias asserts: [[Is 65:20|the child shall die a hundred years old|Puer centum annorum morietur]]. Of old men of this kind it is written in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 8:11|Let not the discourse of the ancients escape thee|Non te prætereat narratio seniorum]]. These die in a good old age, old and full of days [printed as Scripture, with no margin reference; not from Ecclesiasticus 8: compare Gen 25:8 and 1 Par 29:28]. The old women are to be taken in like manner: who may also worthily be called the mothers of others. Of such the Apostle says: [[1 Tim 5:3|Honour widows that are widows indeed|Viduas honora, quæ vere viduæ sunt]]. These, then, shall dwell, that is, shall steadfastly live and remain, [[8:4|in the streets of Jerusalem|in plateis Jerusalem]]: in the divine precepts and counsels, in all the virtues, above all in the charity of God and of the neighbour. By these streets [*plateæ*, broad streets or open squares] one goes to that eternal Jerusalem above the heavens, and arrives there. Hence it is also written in the Psalm: [[Ps 30:9|thou hast set my feet in a spacious place|Statuisti in loco spatioso pedes meos]]; and: [[Ps 118:96|thy commandment is exceeding broad|Latum mandatum tuum nimis]]. The spouse too, in the Canticles, seeks him whom she loves through [[Cant 3:2|the streets and the broad ways|vicos et plateas]]. Nor does it stand in the way that [[Matt 7:14|strait is the way that leadeth to life|arcta est via quæ ducit ad vitam]]: strait it is indeed, because it is hard to persevere in it; and broad, because like a royal road it can take in all, and through charity it reaches out to all men, even to adversaries.

paras.t: Et viri baculus in manu ejus, id est, in horum seniorum manu seu potestate erit virga directionis, paterna correptio, auctoritas prælationis, consolatio et sustentatio infirmorum: idque conveniet eis præ multitudine dierum, id est merito sanctæ conversationis quam tempore longo duxerunt. Unde Apostolus non vult neophytum ordinari episcopum. Propter quod Moyses dixit: Date ex vobis viros sapientes et gnaros, quorum conversatio sit probata in tribus vestris, et ponam eos vobis principes. Et de reprobo populo Dominus in Isaia loquitur: Dabo pueros principes eorum, et effeminati dominabuntur eis.
paras.en: [[8:4|and every man with his staff in his hand|Et viri baculus in manu ejus]], that is, in the hand or power of these elders there shall be the rod of direction, fatherly correction, the authority of prelacy, the consolation and support of the weak: and this shall befit them [[8:4|through multitude of days|præ multitudine dierum]], that is, by the merit of the holy life which they have led for a long time. Hence the Apostle does not want a neophyte to be ordained bishop[[1 Tim 3:6||]]. For which reason Moses said: [[Deut 1:13|Let me have from among you wise and understanding men, and such whose conversation is approved among your tribes, that I may appoint them your rulers|Date ex vobis viros sapientes et gnaros, quorum conversatio sit probata in tribus vestris, et ponam eos vobis principes]]. And of the reprobate people the Lord says in Isaias: [[Is 3:4|I will give children to be their princes, and the effeminate shall rule over them|Dabo pueros principes eorum, et effeminati dominabuntur eis]].

paras.t: Et plateæ civitatis, id est mandata Ecclesiæ, complebuntur infantibus et puellis, id est innocentibus simplicibus, qui juxta Christi doctrinam conversi sunt, et facti ut parvuli: quibus dicit et Paulus, Nolite pueri effici sensibus, sed malitia parvuli estote; et Petrus in prima sua Canonica, Deponentes omnem malitiam et omnem dolum, et simulationes et invidias, quasi modo geniti infantes rationabiles, lac concupiscite; ludentibus in plateis ejus, id est in divinorum præceptorum observantiis cordialiter gloriantibus, atque internam lætitiam gestu corporali monstrantibus: sicut et David testatur, Ludam, et ero humilis in oculis meis. Denique et Sapientia ait in Proverbiorum libro: Delectabar per singulos dies, ludens coram Domino omni tempore, ludens in orbe terrarum. Insuper spiritualis recreatio et ludus ad eutrapeliam pertinens, competit istis pro causa, loco, et tempore.
paras.en: [[8:5|And the streets of the city|Et plateæ civitatis]], that is, the commandments of the Church, [[8:5|shall be full of boys and girls|complebuntur infantibus et puellis]], that is, of the innocent and simple, who according to the teaching of Christ have been converted and become as little children[[Matt 18:3||]]: to whom Paul too says: [[1 Cor 14:20|do not become children in sense. But in malice be children|Nolite pueri effici sensibus, sed malitia parvuli estote]]; and Peter in his first canonical Epistle: [[1 Pet 2:1|laying away all malice and all guile and dissimulations and envies|Deponentes omnem malitiam et omnem dolum, et simulationes et invidias]], [[1 Pet 2:2|As newborn babes, desire the rational milk|quasi modo geniti infantes rationabiles, lac concupiscite]] [Denis's text reads *rationabiles*, so that it is the babes, not the milk, that are rational]; [[8:5|playing in the streets thereof|ludentibus in plateis ejus]], that is, glorying from the heart in the keeping of the divine precepts, and showing their inward gladness by bodily gesture: as David too bears witness: [[2 Kings 6:22|I will both play|Ludam]], [[2 Kings 6:22|and I will be little in my own eyes|et ero humilis in oculis meis]]. Lastly, Wisdom too says in the book of Proverbs: [[Prov 8:30|was delighted every day, playing before him at all times|Delectabar per singulos dies, ludens coram Domino omni tempore]], [[Prov 8:31|Playing in the world|ludens in orbe terrarum]]. Moreover, spiritual recreation and play belonging to eutrapelia [that is, the virtue of seemly mirth and pleasantry in recreation] befit these, as cause, place and time allow.

paras.t: Hæc dicit Dominus: Si difficile videbitur in oculis reliquiarum populi hujus, id est, licet reformatio Ecclesiæ, et multiplicatio fidelium videatur impossibilis, aut multum difficilis bonis Christianis perpaucis, propter nimium lapsum fidelium; numquid in oculis meis difficile erit? Non plane, quia non erit impossibile apud Deum omne verbum. Non ergo de reformatione Ecclesiæ desperemus, sed quo major est ejus indigentia ac ruina, eo instantius atque ferventius divinæ pietatis imploremus suffragia.
paras.en: [[8:6|Thus saith the Lord|Hæc dicit Dominus]]: [[8:6|If it seem hard in the eyes of the remnant of this people|Si difficile videbitur in oculis reliquiarum populi hujus]], that is, although the reform of the Church and the multiplying of the faithful may seem impossible, or very hard, to the very few good Christians, because of the excessive falling away of the faithful: [[8:6|shall it be hard in my eyes|numquid in oculis meis difficile erit]]? Plainly not, because [[Luke 1:37|no word shall be impossible with God|non erit impossibile apud Deum omne verbum]]. Let us not, then, despair of the reform of the Church; but the greater her need and her ruin, the more urgently and fervently let us implore the help of the divine mercy.

paras.t: Hæc dicit Dominus: Ecce ego salvabo populum meum de terra orientis, et de terra occasus solis. Ubique novit Dominus qui sunt ejus; et salvantur quicumque præordinati sunt ad vitam æternam.
paras.en: [[8:7|Thus saith the Lord|Hæc dicit Dominus]]: [[8:7|Behold I will save my people from the land of the east, and from the land of the going down of the sun|Ecce ego salvabo populum meum de terra orientis, et de terra occasus solis]]. Everywhere [[2 Tim 2:19|the Lord knoweth who are his|novit Dominus qui sunt ejus]]; and saved are [[Acts 13:48|as many as were ordained to life everlasting|quicumque præordinati sunt ad vitam æternam]].

paras.t: Confortentur manus vestræ, et indefessi in operibus bonis estote, qui auditis in his diebus sermones istos de reformatione Ecclesiæ promissionibusque divinis, et animarum profectu, per os Prophetarum, id est a prædicatoribus atque doctoribus, ceterisque devotis, futurum Dei judicium, ac omnium venturam finalem remunerationem jugiter vobis narrantibus (de quibus ad Corinthios scribit Apostolus: Prophetæ duo vel tres dicant, et ceteri dijudicent), in die qua fundata est domus Domini, id est, animæ vestræ esse cœperunt domus, templum ac thalamus Sponsi cœlestis, per fidem formatam et gratiæ infusionem, ut templum ædificaretur, id est, per opera virtuosa continuata vos ipsi consecraremini in templum Spiritus Sancti: sicut ait Apostolus, Templum Dei sanctum est, quod estis vos.
paras.en: [[8:9|Let your hands be strengthened|Confortentur manus vestræ]], and be unwearied in good works, [[8:9|you that hear in these days these words|qui auditis in his diebus sermones istos]] about the reform of the Church, the divine promises and the progress of souls, [[8:9|by the mouth of the prophets|per os Prophetarum]], that is, from preachers and doctors and other devout persons, who continually tell you of the judgment of God to come and of the final reward that awaits all (of whom the Apostle writes to the Corinthians: [[1 Cor 14:29|let the prophets speak, two or three: and let the rest judge|Prophetæ duo vel tres dicant, et ceteri dijudicent]]), [[8:9|in the day that the house of the Lord of hosts was founded|in die qua fundata est domus Domini]], that is, your souls began to be the house, the temple and the bridal chamber of the heavenly Bridegroom, through formed faith [that is, faith given its form, its life, by charity] and the infusion of grace, [[8:9|that the temple might be built|ut templum ædificaretur]], that is, that by virtuous works kept up without a break you yourselves might be consecrated into a temple of the Holy Ghost: as the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 3:17|the temple of God is holy, which you are|Templum Dei sanctum est, quod estis vos]].

paras.t: Siquidem ante dies illos, id est, antequam domus Dei modo præfato initiaretur in vobis, merces hominum non erat, nec merces jumentorum, id est, nec litterati, nec idiotæ aliquid meritorie operabantur, quoniam caritate infusa (quæ est animæ vita) carebant, et sine gratia nihil futuræ beatitudinis promeretur natura; neque introeunti, neque exeunti erat pax, id est vera mentis tranquillitas in Deo, præ tribulatione, id est vitiorum inordinatione et confusione. Animus quippe inordinatus, sibi ipsi pœnosus est: sicut et vir eruditus, in Deo tranquillus, suavis est animæ suæ. Et dimisi omnes homines, unumquemque contra proximum suum. Quum enim caritas et gratia deest, mox oriuntur ex amore privati lites, contentiones, discordiæ, et cetera opera carnis.
paras.en: [[8:10|For before those days|Siquidem ante dies illos]], that is, before the house of God was begun in you in the manner just described, [[8:10|there was no hire for men, neither was there hire for beasts|merces hominum non erat, nec merces jumentorum]], that is, neither the learned nor the unlettered did anything meritoriously, because they lacked infused charity (which is the life of the soul), and without grace nature merits nothing of the beatitude to come; [[8:10|neither was there peace to him that came in, nor to him that went out|neque introeunti, neque exeunti erat pax]], that is, true tranquillity of mind in God, [[8:10|because of the tribulation|præ tribulatione]], that is, the disorder and confusion of the vices. For a disordered mind is a torment to itself: as, on the other hand, the learned man, tranquil in God, [[Ecclus 37:22|is sweet to his own soul|suavis est animæ suæ]]. [[8:10|and I let all men go every one against his neighbour|Et dimisi omnes homines, unumquemque contra proximum suum]]. For when charity and grace are lacking, there soon arise from private love quarrels, [[Gal 5:20|contentions|contentiones]], discords, and the other [[Gal 5:19|works of the flesh|opera carnis]].

paras.t: Nunc autem, quum domum conscientiæ mihi præparaverunt, non juxta dies priores, quibus sine gratia exsistentes, sine mercede fuerunt, ego faciam reliquiis populi hujus, id est residuis Christianis; sed semen pacis erit, id est filii pacis atque pacifice mutuo conversantes. Vinea, id est Ecclesia: de qua ait in Evangelio Christus, Homo quidam plantavit vineam: de qua scriptum est in Canticis, Vinea fuit Pacifico; dabit fructum suum, id est, in bonis operibus fructuosa erit, ut dicere queat: Ego autem sicut oliva fructifera. Vel vinea ista est Christus, qui ait, Ego sum vitis vera: qui dedit et dat fructum, spirituales filios generando, et de plenitudine suæ gratiæ ceteris influendo, suumque meritum nobis per sacramenta applicando et communicando.
paras.en: [[8:11|But now|Nunc autem]], when they have prepared for me the house of their conscience, [[8:11|I will not deal with the remnant of this people|ego faciam reliquiis populi hujus]], that is, with the Christians that remain, [[8:11|according to the former days|non juxta dies priores]], in which, being without grace, they were without hire; [[8:12|But there shall be the seed of peace|sed semen pacis erit]], that is, sons of peace, living peaceably with one another. [[8:12|the vine|Vinea]], that is, the Church, of which Christ says in the Gospel: [[Luke 20:9|A certain man planted a vineyard|Homo quidam plantavit vineam]]; of which it is written in the Canticles: [[Cant 8:11|The peaceable had a vineyard|Vinea fuit Pacifico]]; [[8:12|shall yield her fruit|dabit fructum suum]], that is, she shall be fruitful in good works, so that she may say: [[Ps 51:10|But I, as a fruitful olive tree|Ego autem sicut oliva fructifera]]. Or this vine is Christ, who says: [[John 15:1|I am the true vine|Ego sum vitis vera]]; who has given and gives fruit, by begetting spiritual sons, by pouring of the fullness of his grace into others, and by applying and imparting his merit to us through the sacraments.

paras.t: Et terra dabit germen suum. Terra ista sunt, de quibus ait Salvator: Quod autem in terram bonam cecidit, hi sunt qui audientes verbum Dei, corde bono et optimo retinent, et afferunt fructum in patientia. Quum ergo Dominus benignitatem dat gratiæ suæ, terra nostra dat fructum suum. Et cæli dabunt rorem suum: id est, viri spirituales et contemplativi, prædicatores verbi Dei, verba eruditionis et consolationis auditoribus suis infundent, et corda eorum irrigabunt, ac fecundabunt.
paras.en: [[8:12|and the earth shall give her increase|Et terra dabit germen suum]]. This earth is those of whom the Saviour says: [[Luke 8:15|that on the good ground are they who in a good and perfect heart, hearing the word, keep it and bring forth fruit in patience|Quod autem in terram bonam cecidit, hi sunt qui audientes verbum Dei, corde bono et optimo retinent, et afferunt fructum in patientia]]. When, therefore, the Lord gives the goodness of his grace, [[Ps 84:13|our earth shall yield her fruit|terra nostra dat fructum suum]]. [[8:12|and the heavens shall give their dew|Et cæli dabunt rorem suum]]: that is, spiritual and contemplative men, preachers of the word of God, will pour words of instruction and consolation into their hearers, and will water their hearts and make them fruitful.

paras.t: Et erit: Sicut eratis maledictio in gentibus, domus Juda et domus Israel, sic salvabo vos, et eritis benedictio. Frequenter contingit, ut aliqui Christiani, sive sæculares, sive religiosi, et præsertim religiosi et clerici, qui ad perfectiorem vitam tenentur, suis exigentibus vitiis, gratia Dei priventur, et deinceps valde reprehensibiliter conversentur, atque ob id ab aliis contemnantur et maledicantur. Quumque clementia Dei ad virtuosam vitam reduxerit eos, eatenus se emendant, ut alii ædificentur et benedicant eisdem. Ideo Petrus inducit: Abstinete a carnalibus desideriis, quæ militant adversus animam, conversationem vestram inter gentes habentes bonam, ut in eo quod detrectant de vobis, tanquam de malefactoribus, ex bonis operibus vos considerantes, glorificent Deum. Et rursus: Hæc est, inquit, voluntas Dei, ut obmutescere faciatis imprudentium hominum ignorantiam.
paras.en: [[8:13|And it shall come to pass, that as you were a curse among the Gentiles, O house of Juda, and house of Israel: so will I save you, and you shall be a blessing|Et erit: Sicut eratis maledictio in gentibus, domus Juda et domus Israel, sic salvabo vos, et eritis benedictio]]. It often happens that some Christians, whether seculars or religious, and especially religious and clerics, who are bound to a more perfect life, are deprived of the grace of God as their vices deserve, and afterwards live in a very blameworthy way, and for this are despised and cursed by others. And when the mercy of God has brought them back to a virtuous life, they amend themselves so far that others are edified and bless them. Therefore Peter urges you [[1 Pet 2:11|to refrain yourselves from carnal desires which war against the soul|Abstinete a carnalibus desideriis, quæ militant adversus animam]], [[1 Pet 2:12|Having your conversation good among the Gentiles: that whereas they speak against you as evildoers, they may, by the good works which they shall behold in you, glorify God|conversationem vestram inter gentes habentes bonam, ut in eo quod detrectant de vobis, tanquam de malefactoribus, ex bonis operibus vos considerantes, glorificent Deum]]. And again: This, he says, is [[1 Pet 2:15|the will of God|voluntas Dei]], that [[1 Pet 2:15|you may put to silence the ignorance of foolish men|obmutescere faciatis imprudentium hominum ignorantiam]].

paras.t: Cetera ex præcedenti articulo adeo lucide patent, ut hic nihil reiterare oporteat. Verumtamen huic quod nunc ait Propheta, Jejunium quarti, et jejunium quinti, etc., erit domui Juda in gaudium, consonat quod in Matthæo loquitur Christus: Quum jejunatis, nolite fieri sicut hypocritæ, tristes; tu autem quum jejunas, unge caput tuum, et faciem tuam lava, ne videaris hominibus jejunans, sed Patri tuo qui est in abscondito. Docemur quoque ex his, jejunia temporalia, et alia ab Ecclesia instituta atque præcepta, diligenter servare. Non enim sine mortali peccato omittuntur, nisi adsit vere rationabilis causa. Siquidem Deo et Ecclesiæ rectæque rationi pariformiter obedire debemus. Postremo, sic jejunare debet Christianus, ut vitia universa pro viribus vitet. Scriptum est enim: Homo qui jejunat in peccatis suis, et iterum facit ea, quid proficit humiliando se?
paras.en: The rest is so clear from the preceding article that there is no need to repeat anything here. Yet with what the Prophet now says, [[8:19|The fast of the fourth month, and the fast of the fifth|Jejunium quarti, et jejunium quinti]], etc., [[8:19|shall be to the house of Juda, joy|erit domui Juda in gaudium]], there agrees what Christ says in Matthew: [[Matt 6:16|when you fast, be not as the hypocrites, sad|Quum jejunatis, nolite fieri sicut hypocritæ, tristes]]; [[Matt 6:17|But thou, when thou fastest anoint thy head, and wash thy face|tu autem quum jejunas, unge caput tuum, et faciem tuam lava]], [[Matt 6:18|That thou appear not to men to fast, but to thy Father who is in secret|ne videaris hominibus jejunans, sed Patri tuo qui est in abscondito]]. We are taught also by these words to keep diligently the fasts of the seasons [that is, the Ember Days, the fasts of the four seasons of the year], and the other fasts instituted and commanded by the Church. For they are not omitted without mortal sin, unless a truly reasonable cause be present; since we ought to obey God, the Church and right reason alike. Lastly, a Christian ought so to fast that he shuns all vices as far as he can. For it is written: [[Ecclus 34:31|a man that fasteth for his sins, and doth the same again, what doth his humbling himself profit him?|Homo qui jejunat in peccatis suis, et iterum facit ea, quid proficit humiliando se?]]

paras.t: Iterum, quum aliquem justum sensatum et laudabiliter in omnibus se habentem conspicimus, apprehendamus vestem ipsius, dicentes: Ibimus tecum: audivimus enim quoniam Dominus tecum est. Hocque dicendo, sequamur vestigia ejus, seu virtutum exempla. Ideo enim in Ecclesiastico dicitur: Quum videris sensatum, statim evigila ad illum; et, Cum viro sancto assiduus esto.
paras.en: Again, when we see some just man, of good understanding and bearing himself praiseworthily in all things, let us take hold of his garment, saying: [[8:23|We will go with you|Ibimus tecum]]: [[8:23|for we have heard that God is with you|audivimus enim quoniam Dominus tecum est]] [Denis has *with thee* and *the Lord*, fitting the words to one man]. And saying this, let us follow his footsteps, that is, the examples of his virtues. For this is why it is said in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 6:36|if thou see a man of understanding, go to him early in the morning|Quum videris sensatum, statim evigila ad illum]]; and: [[Ecclus 37:15|be continually with a holy man|Cum viro sancto assiduus esto]].
